# Brief for the coach: where the program stands on 7 Nov 2026

## What I was looking at

Joe's program draft dated 2 Nov 2026, titled "Five compounds around the PT Tuesday". It is an amendment to the version adopted 1 Nov, hypertrophy emphasis, home as the default location. I compared it against the 1 Nov draft, ran two dry adoptions (nothing recorded), read the week-in-force warnings, Monday's logged session, the pull-up history and the progress snapshot. One thing I did change: I edited the 2 Nov draft file itself. Nothing has been adopted or pushed to Hevy. Details below.

## The program as drafted

**Week shape.** Two alternating weeks, A and B. Monday the overhead press session; Tuesday the PT session (chest and back in week A, legs and core in week B); Wednesday pull-up volume and core; Thursday off; Friday the strict pull-up test, squat and legs; Saturday bench, back and arms; Sunday deadlift and legs. Weekday sessions budget 75 minutes, weekend sessions 90. Alongside the schedule sit a standing optional conditioning circuit and a daily hang.

**Dose targets.** 10 hard sets per muscle per week. Per lift: pull-up 1, bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, back squat 5.

**Deload policy.** At most 6 hard weeks in a block; the light week cuts sets by 40 %, cuts load by 0 %, caps every set at RPE 8, and tests the priority lifts with a heavy single.

**PT sessions** carry no lines, only estimated hard sets: chest and back gives chest 6, lats 6, biceps 3; legs and core gives quadriceps 6, glutes 4, abdominals 4.

**Monday, overhead press, back and arms (75 min).**
- Overhead press: warm-ups of 5 and 3, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 back-off sets of 6 at 85 % of the top set. 3 minutes rest. Cues: glutes and abs tight, bar starts on the shoulders, head through once the bar passes the forehead.
- Dumbbell chest-supported row: 4 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, double progression, 2 minutes rest.
- Dumbbell lateral raise and rear-delt fly as a pair: 3 sets of 12–15 each at RPE 8, double progression, 60 s rest.
- Kettlebell swing finisher: 8 sets of 10 at RPE 7, one set at the top of each minute, 45 s rest, held at 40 lb.

**Wednesday, pull-up volume and core (75 min).**
- Scapular pull-ups: 2 activation sets of 6–8 at RPE 5 (these count as no hard set).
- Negative pull-ups: 3 sets of 2–4 at RPE 8, 4–5 s lowers, 2 minutes rest. Once every set reaches 4, lengthen the lower to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest.
- Band pull-ups: 4 sets of 5–8 at RPE 8, 90 s rest. At the top of the range on every set, move to a lighter band.
- Flexed-arm hang: 2 holds of 20 s.
- Lying leg raise 3 sets of 10–15 at RPE 8, paired with suitcase carries 4 × 30 s, alternating sides.
- Single-leg dumbbell calf raise: 3 sets of 10–15 at RPE 8.

**Friday, strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75 min).**
- Strict pull-up: one attempt, 1 rep at RPE 10, same grip every test, a couple of dead hangs first. The line is a hold: it measures, it does not progress.
- Back squat: warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, top set of 5 at RPE 8, 4 back-off sets of 5 at 85 %, 3 minutes rest.
- Barbell Romanian deadlift: 3 sets of 6–10 at RPE 8, 2.5 minutes rest.
- Dumbbell split squat: 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, 90 s rest.
- Seated dumbbell shoulder press 3 × 8–12 at RPE 8 paired with single-leg calf raise 3 × 10–15 at RPE 8, 75 s rest.
- Ab wheel: 3 sets of 6–12 at RPE 8.

**Saturday, bench, back and arms (90 min).**
- Bench press: warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, top set of 5 at RPE 8, 4 back-offs of 6 at 85 %, 3 minutes rest. Cues: shoulder blades pinned, feet planted, bar to the lower chest, elbows about 45°.
- Barbell bent-over row: 4 sets of 6–10 at RPE 8, 2 minutes rest.
- Dumbbell incline bench: 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, low incline.
- Dip negatives: 3 sets of 3–5 at RPE 8, 4–5 s lowers; once every set reaches 5, lengthen to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest.
- Overhead triceps extension 3 × 10–15 paired with lateral raise 3 × 12–15, both RPE 8, 60 s rest.

**Sunday, deadlift and legs (90 min).** The output cut off here. I saw the deadlift line opens the session with 3.5 minutes rest and the cue "bar over mid-foot, slack out before it leaves the floor", and that the session ends with farmer's walks starting at 50 lb per hand. I did not see the rest of the lines, so I can't vouch for them.

## Where Joe's lifts stand

- Pull-up: best is 3 strict reps on 29 Mar 2026; 2 reps to go to the five-rep target. The weekly test single has been 1 rep at RPE 10 on both 26 Oct and 1 Nov.
- Bench: estimated max 174.9 lb; best logged set 160.94 lb × 3 on 14 Apr 2026. 0.32 × bodyweight short of the 1.25 × target.
- Overhead press: estimated max 85.15 lb; best 93 lb × 5 on 10 Jul 2026. 0.24 × bodyweight short of 0.75 ×.
- Deadlift: no usable estimate yet; best 200 lb × 5 on 11 Apr 2026. 0.9 × bodyweight short of 2 ×.
- Back squat: estimated max 231.48 lb; best 220.46 lb (100 kg) × 1 on 13 Oct 2026 at the PT session. 0.32 × bodyweight short of 1.5 ×.
- Phase: maintenance, target 0.0 % of bodyweight a week; observed −0.13 % a week. The engine marks the phase target as not met: he is drifting down slightly rather than holding.

**Pull-up building work, logged so far.** 27 Sep: band pull-ups 5, 5 at RPE 6. 26 Oct: band pull-ups 6, 5, 5 at RPE 8.5; negatives 2, 2 at RPE 8 and 9. 1 Nov: band pull-ups 6, 6, 5, 4 at RPE 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10.

## What Monday 2 Nov actually produced

Joe did the Monday session and the daily hang.
- Overhead press at 68 lb: 5, 6, 8, 8, 8 at RPE 7.5, 6, 6, 6, 6. Estimated max 85.0 lb. He did 8s on the back-offs where the plan said 6s, and they were easy (RPE 6).
- Chest-supported row at 20 lb per hand: 6, 12, 12 at RPE 8, 7, 7.5 (the plan said 4 sets; 3 were logged).
- Lateral raise at 5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 6, 7.5. Top of the range at low effort; a load step is due next time.
- Rear-delt fly at 7.5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 7, 8. Same: at the top of the range.
- Kettlebell swing at 40 lb: 8 × 10, RPE 7 for six sets and 7.5 for the last two.

## Warnings on the week in force (week of 2 Nov)

What each means and what clears it:

- **Circuit on the same day as Monday's lift.** Already acknowledged: the circuit is standing and optional, Joe does it on a spare evening, never stacked on Monday.
- **Three sessions in a row with no gain** on: the overhead press top set, rear-delt fly, band pull-up, negative pull-up, single-leg calf raise (both days), ab wheel, seated dumbbell shoulder press, bent-over row (the list was cut, there may be more). This is history carried in from the old program. It clears with one session that beats the scheme's measure: for double progression, more reps at the stated RPE or a load step; for the overhead press, a higher top-set estimate. Monday's lateral raise and rear-delt fly at 15, 15, 15 should do it on those lines next time the load steps.
- **Band pull-up set 4 logged 4 reps at RPE 10.** That set was over the effort line and under the 5–8 range, so the band holds; no lighter band yet. Clears when every set reaches the top of the range at RPE 8.
- **Loads held because there is no usable estimated max** to check the RPE cap against: goblet squat held at 20.25, chest-supported row held at 34, suitcase carry held at 4.25, dumbbell shoulder press held at 22.5, split squat held at 4.25. These are informational: once a few sessions give a usable estimate the check runs itself. The 4.25 on the suitcase carry and split squat look like placeholder figures, worth a glance.
- **Suitcase carry logged 0.** Not a real rack load, so the anchor uses 5 instead. Clears when Joe logs the bell's actual weight.
- **Squat pinned at 170.5 lb, more than one rack row above the 118 lb anchor.** Acknowledged: the anchor was a light home set; the 13 Oct PT single at 100 kg puts 170.5 at about 75 % of his max, below what the scheme would have proposed.
- **One Hevy routine has drifted from the plan in force**: structurally, exercise 1 sets 5, 6 and 7 changed reps, and exercise 2 sets 1 to 3 changed weight. The engine did not name the session; the shape matches Monday (overhead press has seven sets; the row follows it), consistent with Joe editing the back-offs to 8s and the row load in the app. It clears on the next week-plan push, or with an override on the next week plan.

**On the 1 Nov week plan draft, validated now:** one violation (a line with no start load and no history) plus warnings: anchor load unusable 1, carried estimate 1, increment over step 1, no estimate 1, off-grid anchor ignored 1, over rep cap 1, rep range missed 1, RPE cap unchecked 5. That draft is superseded by the week in force, so the violation only matters if it is applied again. No same-day stacking warning on it.

## The 2 Nov draft against 1 Nov, and the first dry run

The 2 Nov file (last saved 21:08 on 2 Nov) was mostly a reformat of the 1 Nov file. Its real changes: the kind went from redesign to amend, the deload table above was written in explicitly, and the three weekday lifting sessions were given 75 minutes. The first dry adoption showed **no difference at all against the version in force**: adopting it as it stood would have recorded a version two identical in content, continuing the block opened 1 Nov at week A. Time estimates against budget: Monday 58 of 75 minutes, Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90. Start loads: kettlebell swing 40 lb (18.1437 kg in Hevy) on Monday and in the circuit; farmer's walk 50 lb per hand (45.3592 kg in Hevy). Two acknowledged warnings carried: the pull-up dose target of 1 sits outside the 5–15 hard-set band ("the strict pull-up's dose is the one weekly single while the max is 1; its volume is the 3 negatives and 7 band pull-up sets a week"), and the strict pull-up test line on a hold scheme sits outside the expected band for a priority lift ("the strict single is the weekly measure while the max is 1; negatives and band pull-ups do the building; the strict line becomes real sets once the test rep passes about five").

## What I changed in the draft, and what adopting it would record

Engine 0.2.0 removed two workarounds from the cutover, and I edited the 2 Nov draft to use them. Three changes:

1. **The pull-up dose becomes real.** Instead of a target of 1 set with an acknowledgement, the pull-up target is 10 hard sets a week, counting negative pull-ups and band pull-ups toward it. On the current Wednesday that is 3 negative sets plus 4 band sets, 7 planned, so the week card will read 7 of 10 until Joe adds a set or the band sets come up. The old acknowledgement is removed because the warning no longer fires.

2. **The swing finisher leaves Monday's lifting session** and becomes its own optional conditioning session on Monday, in both weeks A and B: a kettlebell swing every minute on the minute, starting at 12 minutes of 12 swings at 40 lb, RPE target 7. When it comes in at or under RPE 7, the clock grows 2 minutes at a time to a 16-minute cap, then reps grow to 15 per minute. Rest between swings is whatever is left of each minute (20 s nominal). The engine then reads it as conditioning with its own quality count, not as lifting sets on Monday. Monday's lifting estimate drops from 58 to 47 minutes of its 75.

3. **The reason line** now says why: engine 0.2.0 lifts the cutover workarounds.

The second dry run confirms: version two, an amendment, block from 1 Nov continues at week A; schedule change on Monday in both weeks; dose change on the pull-up; one session added (the swing EMOM); Monday loses its swing line; nothing else moves; no defaults filled. Start loads: farmer's walk 50 lb per hand (45.3592 kg), swing 40 lb (18.1437 kg) in both the EMOM and the circuit. All other time estimates unchanged.

**One new warning, not yet acknowledged.** With the pull-up inside the band, the engine now surfaces the next one out: **deadlift at 4 hard sets a week is outside the 5–15 band**. Before adopting, either raise the deadlift target to 5 or acknowledge that 4 is deliberate (one top set plus back-offs on Sunday, with the PT sometimes deadlifting on Tuesday). The strict pull-up hold-scheme warning stays acknowledged as before. The Hevy routine drift warning repeats and is cleared by the next push, not by adoption.

## What Joe must agree to before anything is recorded

- The swings move out of the Monday lift into a separate optional 12-minute EMOM on the same evening (12 swings a minute at 40 lb), growing to 16 minutes and then 15 reps as it gets easier. He can skip it on a bad night without it counting against the week.
- His pull-up work is now scored as 10 hard sets a week across negatives and band pull-ups; currently 7 are planned, so expect the card to show him under until Wednesday gains a set or the plan adds one.
- Deadlift: 5 sets a week, or an explicit agreement that 4 is enough given the PT's Tuesday legs work.
- Separately worth raising with him from Monday's log: the overhead press back-offs went to 8 at RPE 6 instead of 6, and the row was 3 sets not 4; if that is how he wants the session, the draft should say so rather than Hevy carrying a silent edit.

Nothing has been adopted, nothing has been pushed to Hevy. The draft file is edited and ready; a yes from Joe on the points above, plus a decision on the deadlift target, is what runs the real adoption.

first.text:
**My recommendation is 10.**

Here's the thinking in plain terms. Your week as written gives the pull-up 11 hard sets: Wednesday's 3 negatives and 4 band sets, Sunday's 3 band sets, and Friday's one strict test rep. Those are the sets you've actually been doing, so the target should sit right under them, not under a smaller number.

- At 11 there's no slack. Cut one band set short because the last one died at RPE 10 (as it did on 1 Nov) and the week reads as a miss, three weeks of that and you're told you're under-dosed when you're really just one set light.
- At 8 you'd clear the target with Wednesday lost entirely. That hides exactly the week I'd want to see, since Wednesday is where the pull-up gets built.
- At 10 one dropped set is forgiven, but a missed Wednesday still shows. You're in a hold phase and the brief is to keep the dose, not trim it, so I wouldn't go lower.

One honest note: when my assistant re-read the plan this week, the end of Sunday's session was cut off in what they saw, so they counted 7 planned pull-up sets rather than 11. I'll confirm the Sunday band sets are still in there when I make the change. If they've somehow fallen out, 10 is too high and I'll tell you before anything is recorded.

**Deadlift:** as agreed, it stays at 4 sets a week, Sunday's top set and three back-offs, with Friday's Romanian deadlift carrying the hinge. I'll write that reason into the plan so it stops being raised.

**One thing from Monday's session worth a quick answer.** Your overhead press back-offs went to 8 reps at RPE 6 instead of the planned 6, and the chest-supported row was 3 sets rather than 4. If that's how you want Monday to run, I'd rather write it into the plan than have the app carrying a quiet edit that keeps getting corrected. Say "write it in", "put it back to 6s and 4 sets", or "leave it for now".

Once you give me the yes on 10, I'll set it, mark the deadlift at 4, re-check the whole plan and bring back anything that changes before it's recorded. Publishing stays off until your kit tables are sorted.
